baseline.title: Baseline (nothing happens)
baseline.description: Continuous average diet (2.1 L/day water, 150 mmol/day Na, 80 mmol/day K). The model should sit exactly at its steady state.

validation.summary: All states remain at the analytic steady state (numerical drift only).

drink_water_1L.title: Drink 1 L of water in 10 min
drink_water_1L.description: 1 L plain water over 10 min at t = 1 h.

validation.summary: Plasma Na dips ~2-4 mmol/L, ADH is suppressed, urine dilutes toward ~50-70 mOsm/kg, water diuresis peaks ~1-2 h after drinking and the load is largely excreted within ~3-4 h.

expects.note: Spec §8. Baylis: sustained water load lowered osmolality ~7 mOsm/kg (≈ −3.5 mmol/L Na).

expects.metric: time to recover |ΔNa| < 0.5 mmol/L after drinking starts
time of peak urine flow after drinking starts

expects.target: ≈0.5-0.8 L/h (Shafiee 11 mL/min for ~1.4 L; Crowe ~0.76 L/h for 20 mL/kg)
expects.note: Literature loads were ~1.4 L, so a 1 L load is expected at or below their peak.

expects.metric: fraction of the 1 L excreted (above baseline urine) by 3 h after drinking
expects.target: most of it (Crowe: ~100% of 20 mL/kg in 2 h in young water-replete men)

drink_water_3L_fast.title: Drink 3 L of water in 30 min (hyponatremia risk demo)
drink_water_3L_fast.description: 3 L plain water over 30 min at t = 1 h. Shows where plasma Na crosses the 135 mmol/L hyponatremia boundary.

validation.summary: Intake rate (6 L/h) far exceeds maximal free-water excretion (~0.7 L/h), so plasma Na falls several mmol/L and can cross 135 mmol/L (hyponatremia by EAH consensus definition) before the kidney clears the load.

expects.target: demonstrated in median trajectory (model behaviour, not a validated human threshold)

salt_load_10g.title: Eat 10 g salt (171 mmol Na) with 0.5 L water
salt_load_10g.description: Oral NaCl load 10 g (171 mmol Na) with 0.5 L water over 15 min at t=1 h, on top of baseline diet.

validation.summary: Plasma Na rises ~1-3 mmol/L, ADH and thirst rise, urine concentrates, ECF expands by water drawn from cells, and the extra Na is excreted only gradually over ~24-48 h.

expects.note: Spec §8. Suckling 2012: +3.13 ± 0.75 after 6 g in soup vs matched unsalted soup (SEM vs SD unverified; context only, not the source of this band); Andersen 1999: +2.7 after IV hypertonic load ≈10% ECF Na.
Andersen 2002: AVP 1.4 -> 3.1 pg/mL after hypertonic NaCl.

expects.metric: fraction of the 171 mmol load excreted (above baseline) by 8 h
expects.target: ≈25% (Andersen 1999 IV load: 131 vs 81 mmol in 8 h)
expects.note: IV not oral; supine; time-control also rose. Loose band.
Spec §5 expectation; the multi-day rhythmicity reported by the Titze group is not modelled.

salt_load_sweep.title: Salt dose sweep 0-30 g (how much salt strains the kidney?)
salt_load_sweep.description: Single oral NaCl loads from 0 to 30 g (each with 0.5 L water) at t = 1 h; 48 h per dose. The default inputs() is the 10 g member so the object is also directly simulatable.

validation.summary: Peak kidney strain index, peak Δ[Na], peak ECF expansion and 24 h Na excretion should increase monotonically with dose. The strain index is a model index, not a clinical measure.

expects.metric: Context, not checked on this chart: 6 g salted minus matched-water control
expects.target: +3.13 ± 0.75 mmol/L (Suckling 2012; SEM/SD unverified). This chart shows the rise from each person's own baseline, a different quantity; status: unverified, not counted as a pass
expects.note: Audit F-02/F-03 (BUG-0050, BUG-0051). The salted-minus-control comparison is a skipped test in tests/engine.test.mjs until the dispersion is confirmed from the full text.

chronic_high_salt_30d.title: Chronic high salt: 15 g/day for 30 days
chronic_high_salt_30d.description: Diet salt raised from 8.8 g/day (150 mmol) to 15 g/day (257 mmol) at t = 24 h and held for 30 days. MODELED RISK TRAJECTORY, NOT A PREDICTION.

validation.summary: Na balance re-establishes within days at a slightly expanded ECF; MAP rises by a few mmHg over 2–4 weeks as slow whole-body autoregulation (state R_auto, decision D-2) adds to the pressure-natriuresis loop (Guyton/Hall), then plateaus.

expects.metric: ΔMAP at day 30 per +100 mmol/day Na
expects.note: MAP band derived from He 2013 normotensive SBP/DBP CIs (MAP ≈ DBP + (SBP−DBP)/3), scaled from 75 to 100 mmol/day. Scaling uses the normotensive subgroup's own urinary Na change, −75 mmol/24 h (BMJ full text, Results, read 2026-10-01; equal to the all-trial value, so the band is unchanged). Still approximate: combining SBP and DBP CI end-points is not a true MAP CI (audit F-06, BUG-0054). Parameters map_vol_exp, pn_gain, aldo_vol_exp were chosen with this target in mind (calibration, not independent validation).

expects.target: still rising at day 14; ≥ 95 % of plateau by day 30; < 60 % of plateau by day 3
expects.note: Decision D-2. Context: He 2013 trials measured BP after ≥ 4 weeks; Guyton 1972 long-term autoregulation acts over days to weeks. map_auto_tau_h was chosen for this shape (calibration, not independent validation). Test: tests/engine.test.mjs "chronic high salt: MAP still rising at day 14".
Steady-state balance is a structural property of the renal-body-fluid feedback.

expects.target: model expands ECF (Guyton). Heer 2000 found plasma volume +315 mL but NO total body water gain at very high intake — known divergence (no Na storage compartment in V1).

chronic_high_salt_30d.label: modeled risk trajectory — not a prediction

no_water_24h.title: No water for 24 h
no_water_24h.description: Drinking water removed for 24 h (t = 1 to 25 h); food Na/K continue; metabolic water continues.

validation.summary: Plasma osmolality and Na rise, ADH rises, urine concentrates toward its maximum, urine flow falls, thirst rises; ECF and ICF both shrink.

expects.target: rise of a few mOsm/kg (qualitative; full-text values not verified)
